criteria.criterion: tools/agent-eval is package main, run as `go run ./tools/agent-eval` from the repository root, with the flags --agent, --model, --out, --cases (default plugin/evals), --case (a path.Match glob, repeatable, a case runs when any matches; every case when absent), --runs (default 1), --judge-model (default sonnet), --timeout (a Go duration, default 20m), --vloop (default the vloop on PATH) and --list.
criteria.evidence: main.go:36-46 defines all flags with the stated defaults; --case uses path.Match over a repeatable multi flag

criteria.criterion: The cases are the directories of --cases whose name does not start with `_`, in name order.
criteria.evidence: cases.go caseNames skips _ prefixes, non-dirs, sorts

criteria.criterion: Before running anything, the first condition that holds, in this order, prints one line on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 2: --agent, --model, --out missing (in that order) → `agent-eval: --<flag> is required`; an agent other than claude or copilot → `agent-eval: unknown agent <a>`; --runs below 1 or not a number → `agent-eval: --runs must be 1 or more`; --timeout not a Go duration → `agent-eval: --timeout <v> is not a duration`; --out exists and is not empty → `agent-eval: <dir> is not empty` (the dir as given); no case matches → `agent-eval: no case matches`; --agent copilot and no vloop binary found (--vloop naming no file, or no vloop binary on PATH) → `agent-eval: no vloop binary for the fence hook`. A refusal writes nothing into an existing --out.
criteria.evidence: main.go checkFlags and run apply the refusals in the stated order, writing nothing; TestRefusalsInOrder covers each and the order

criteria.criterion: --list needs no --agent, --model or --out; it prints a header CASE, PHASE, GRADERS and one line per selected case (its name; its phase, `-` when it has none; its number of graders/*.md), columns aligned with text/tabwriter, padding 2, and exits 0. The phase is the first word of prompt.md's body, `/vloop:<skill>`, when the skill is plan, work, review, gate-review, verify or review-brief; any other skill has none.
criteria.evidence: main.go list branch uses tabwriter with padding 2; cases.go phase detection; real run printed the header and rows, exit 0

criteria.criterion: `go run ./tools/agent-eval --list` over plugin/evals exits 0 with a line for every case and nothing on stderr; no file under plugin/evals is changed to make it so (a violation the review rules against).
criteria.evidence: ran it: exit 0, rows listed; git status shows no change under plugin/

criteria.criterion: A case without prompt.md, or a grader file whose frontmatter cannot be read, prints `agent-eval: <case>/<file>: <reason>` on stderr and exits 1, with or without --list, before anything runs.
criteria.evidence: readCase errors are worded <case>/<file>: reason, run returns 1; TestUnreadableCases covers --list and non-list

criteria.criterion: Frontmatter is the text between the first two `---` lines, read by hand, no module added to go.mod: top-level `key: value`; a key with no value followed by lines indented two spaces, each `key: value`, read as a one-level map; values plain, single-quoted (`''` an escaped quote) or double-quoted, otherwise kept as written, backslashes included; a `[...]` value read as a string and unused. Anything else, including a frontmatter that is never closed, is a reading error.
criteria.evidence: frontmatter.go hand parser; go.mod unchanged; TestFrontmatter and TestFrontmatterErrors cover the forms and errors

criteria.criterion: Committed tests in tools/agent-eval (run by the configured go check under `go test ./...`) cover each refusal and its order, --list over a fixture cases directory built in a temporary directory, and the frontmatter reader's forms and errors; a task that adds this behaviour without such tests fails review.
criteria.evidence: main_test.go has the four tests; the go check log shows tools/agent-eval ok

notes: Minor: readCase swallows an unclosed frontmatter in prompt.md (treats it as all body); the brief's error rule names grader files explicitly, so not ruled a bug, but a later task may want to tighten it.
